pr_comments:
Initial benchmark, reading a file with shape: `(12744000, 12)` and the following schema:

```
{'ids': polars.datatypes.Int32,
 'dates': polars.datatypes.Datetime,
 'feature_0': polars.datatypes.Float32,
 'feature_1': polars.datatypes.Float32,
 'feature_2': polars.datatypes.Float32,
 'feature_3': polars.datatypes.Float32,
 'feature_4': polars.datatypes.Float32,
 'feature_5': polars.datatypes.Float32,
 'feature_6': polars.datatypes.Float32,
 'feature_7': polars.datatypes.Float32,
 'feature_8': polars.datatypes.Float32,
 'feature_9': polars.datatypes.Float32}
```

It seems that the parquet reader now is even faster than the pyarrow reader. (Great job @jorgecarleitao :rocket: )

In decreasing performance:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3023000/147000671-b1ec466b-90f6-42f2-bb56-02d86135ea37.png)


It surprised me however that going from pyarrow to polars is so expensive. :thinking:

issue_context.title: add parallel parquet reading
issue_context.body: Example already defined in arrow2 upstream.
comments: it would be nice to expand the parallel processing to JSON as well. Currently the JSON speeds are sub-optimal. 10K records with 15 fields takes approx 5-6 sec on my machine to load, while a CSV with the same content finishes in <200ms.

review_comments: @jorgecarleitao I combined the IO part with the CPU heavy part. This will likely reduce memory pressure as we have a limited amount of threads.
